organization.manage_security_policy: Decide which roles must carry a second factor and how long their holders have to arrange one. Getting it wrong locks colleagues out of the product.
organization.transfer_ownership: Hand the organization over to somebody else: the previous owner keeps their account and loses everything ownership gave them.

team.read: See the teams of the organization and who is in them.
team.create: Start a new team and say what it is there to do.
team.update: Rename a team and change what it is described as.
team.delete: Delete a team — the people stay, the team does not.
team.manage_members: Add people to a team, take them out, and decide who leads it.

invitation.read: See who has been invited, and whether the invitation is still alive.
invitation.create: Invite a new person by email and choose the roles they arrive with.
invitation.resend: Send the invitation letter again, with a fresh link.
invitation.revoke: Call an invitation back before it is accepted — the link stops working.

employee.read: See the personnel directory and open a colleague's card.
employee.view_org_chart: See who reports to whom across the whole organization.

user.suspend: Cut a person off from the product: every session of theirs ends and they can no longer sign in.
user.reactivate: Bring a suspended colleague back to work with the roles they had.
user.reset_mfa: Take somebody's second factor off, so that until they set up a new one the password alone is enough to sign in as them.

role.read: See the roles of the organization and what each of them grants.
role.create: Build a custom role out of permissions you hold yourself.
role.update: Change what a role grants — for everybody holding it, at once.
role.delete: Delete a role: everybody who held it loses what it granted.
role.assign: Give a person a role, and with it every permission that role carries.
role.revoke: Take a role away from a person, and with it everything the role granted.

permission.override_read: Read another person's effective permissions together with the reason written beside each personal exception.
permission.override: Grant or take away a single permission for one person, past their roles and past what those roles say.
